newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Weak gold hits S.African fund manager Coronation.
newsitem.headline: Weak gold hits S.African fund manager Coronation.

text.p: Coronation Asset Management's portfolios suffered in the second quarter as a result of the poor performance of South African gold mining shares, managing director Leon Campher said on Wednesday.
"We strategically positioned ourselves in some mining shares and quite frankly in terms of share price movement it has been a disaster," Campher told Reuters in an interview.
"Our performance has suffered across all of our portfolios. The real hurt came in June...July was not that bad," he said.
The firm's view on the shares, which included Gencor, Randgold and JCI, had been based on the belief that the continuing restructuring of the country's mining industry would unlock share value.
"We were heavy in Gencor because we liked the international expansion, which has paid off."
Gencor successfully launched its metals arm Billiton Plc on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
But it had also looked to African expansion to boost Randgold and local restructuring to bolster other mining companies, which did not pay off.
Campher said two factors which had gone against the bullish view: the collapse of Canadian resource firm Bre-X and the fall in the gold price.
The Bre-X scandal, which involved a Canadian gold mining firm vastly overstating the potential of a gold discovery in Indonesia, came shortly before Randgold Resources listed in London.
"At the time of the Randgold listing the Canadian scam hit and everyone was all of a sudden very cynical about resource companies."
Randgold Resources debuted on the London Stock Exchange on June 26 at $16.75 -- well below the company's aim to offer the stocks between $18 and $23.
Towards the end of June, the gold price also began its descent to its lowest level in twelve years.
Campher said that in light of the poor performance, Coronation planned to hold a series of investment meetings around the country.

"We have set up presentations around the country in early August and we are going to see all the clients and tell them this is what we did, this is why we did it, we still think our view is correct, we are going to hang in there," he said.
"If we find that some of our initial arguments were fundamentally flawed we will tell people that we are bailing out because we got it wrong," Campher said.
"But until then we still believe it is a position that we will hold."
Coronation Asset Management, a division of Coronation Holdings Ltd, had nearly 19 billion rand under management at the end of the second quarter of 1997.
